1. The promise, and the one rule

Role Scout helps you get from a resume to an interview room without ever saying something about you that is not true.

Every score, every tailored resume, every cover letter and every interview answer Role Scout produces is built only from lines you have read and confirmed as true. That confirmation is called attesting. Nothing is added, rounded up, or strengthened. When Role Scout cannot say something truthfully, it refuses and tells you why, rather than guessing.

What Role Scout will never do
  • Invent a skill, a tool, a date, a number or an achievement that your attested lines do not state.
  • Apply for a job on your behalf, fill in an employer's form, or submit anything. Applying is always your own action.
  • Feed you answers during a live interview.
  • Show a score it cannot explain. Every score comes with a plain reason.
  • Store anything from the free resume check, or keep a file the browser extension captures.
  • Use your data to train AI models. Your data is stored in Canada.

3. Getting in: free check, account, phone app

The free resume check (no account)

At /check you can upload a resume and see whether Role Scout can read it before you sign up. It reports the file type, page count, how many lines it found, and shows the first lines it read. Nothing is saved. If you then press Create my account, the same file is waiting on your Upload step.

Creating an account

Full name, email, password. Your resume stays yours; every line needs your attestation before anything uses it. You choose your country of search on the next screen.

Installing Role Scout on your phone

Role Scout works as an app with no app store. On the home page, the card Add Role Scout to your phone installs it (Android and desktop Chrome: press Install; iPhone: Share, then Add to Home Screen). Installed, it opens from an icon, remembers where you were, and stays readable when you are offline.

4. Step 1: Tell us what you are looking for

ControlWhat it does
Country of searchWhich country's postings you see. Canada also switches on NOC codes and the Express Entry level chip.
Target rolesShort phrases such as service desk analyst. Postings whose titles carry these words rank first. Leave empty to see everything in your country.
SeniorityUsed by the scoring model as context, never as a hard filter.
Preferred location (optional)A city or region. The scoring model weighs it as context and may mention it in a match rationale; it never hides postings.
Minimum acceptable salary (optional)A salary floor. Weighed by the scoring model as context, like seniority; never a hard filter.
Email me a daily digest of new matchesOne email at 08:30 on days when new roles score 60 or above for you. Nothing on quiet days. Off means no email.
Save preferencesSaves, and asks the matcher to look again.

5. Step 2: Upload your resume (or your LinkedIn export)

  1. Choose File. PDF, Word (.docx) or your LinkedIn data export (.zip).
  2. Upload. A new version is created every time. Reading takes about a minute; the page updates on its own.
  3. The version row shows Parsed when Role Scout has turned it into lines, or Could not read with a short reason.
LinkedIn export. On LinkedIn, open Settings and Privacy, then Data privacy, then Get a copy of your data, and request the full archive. LinkedIn emails a ZIP, usually within a day. Upload that ZIP here; Role Scout reads your positions, education, skills and certifications and ignores your connections, birth date and street address.
Scanned images. A photo or a scanned PDF has no text layer and cannot be read. Upload the original file, or a fresh export from your word processor.

6. Step 3: Confirm every line and attest

This is the step that makes everything else trustworthy. Read each line as an employer would.

ControlWhat it does
EditCorrect a line before you attest. Only true lines belong here. Save keeps the change, Cancel discards it.
Ask someone to confirm thisRest your mouse on a line and this link appears under it. It sends a link to a former manager or colleague who can confirm that one line is true; their answer travels with your verified resume.
Every line above is trueAttests this version. Attested lines are what every score, tailored resume, letter and interview pack are built from. Lines cannot be edited after this; upload a new version to make changes.
Why lines cannot be edited after attesting. An employer reading your verified resume must know that what they see is what you confirmed. Changing it afterwards would break that promise. Upload a new version instead; every version keeps its own attestation.

7. Step 4: See your matches

Within minutes of attesting, real postings in your country are scored against your attested lines. Every card carries a score and a one line reason.

Reading a match card

  • Score (0 to 100). 50 and above is shown as ready. Below that, the card sits under the line "these roles are a weaker match".
  • Reason line. One sentence in plain words about why the score is what it is.
  • NOC line (Canada). NOC code, official occupation title and TEER level, shown once the posting has been tagged; new postings are tagged nightly. A teal Express Entry level chip appears for TEER 0 to 3, the level Express Entry programs generally require. It is a starting point, not immigration advice.
  • Source. Which board or employer the posting came from, or Supplied by you for postings you added.

Controls

ControlWhat it does
NOC codeFilters your matches to one occupation code. All codes is the default.
Tailor my resume for this roleRewrites your attested resume for this posting, verified line by line. Nothing new is invented. Usually under two minutes.
Generate cover letterWrites a cover letter from your attested resume for this posting, checked claim by claim. Usually under two minutes.
Dismiss / RestoreHides a role, or brings it back from the dismissed filter.
View the postingOpens the original posting in a new tab.
I appliedAdds the role to your applications tracker.
Tailor for a posting you foundPaste any posting (link, title, employer, location, text). It is saved as yours, scored within a minute, and can be tailored like any match. The browser extension fills this form with one click.
Ten tailorings a day. Every seeker gets ten tailorings a day, which is why Role Scout offers each role once even when a board lists it many times.

8. Step 5: Tailor and apply

The tailored resume page

Every line of the tailored resume traces to your attested lines. The integrity strip at the top counts them: reworded, merged, unchanged, and title mapped. Chips down the right edge mark each changed line.

MarkMeaning
RewordedOne attested line rephrased to match the posting's language. Same facts.
MergedTwo or more attested lines combined.
Title mappedA job title from another country rendered as its Canadian equivalent, with your original title kept in parentheses, only when your attested duties support it.
Verified bannerWhich attested version this was verified against, and when. If a newer attested version exists, the page says so and you can tailor again.
Show all sourcesShows the attested lines behind every tailored line.

Downloading and sharing

ControlWhat it does
Download PDF / Download WordDownloads the tailored resume. Word files can be edited.
LayoutClassic is the standard look. Compact fits more on one page. Plain uses Times in black only for the most conservative employers.
Enable sharingCreates a private verification link that shows this resume with its verification to anyone who has the link. You see every open (count and last date).
Get a new linkReplaces the link; the old one stops working.
Turn off sharingThe link stops working immediately.
Apply on the original postingOpens the employer posting. You apply; Role Scout never does.

The coverage report

Below the document, What this posting asks for splits the posting into two columns: evidenced by your attested resume, each point tied to real lines, and not evidenced, the honest gaps. The page says it plainly: closing them in real life is the only way Role Scout will ever show them as evidence. The not evidenced list is carried into your interview pack.

When Role Scout refuses. If the verifier cannot confirm a tailored line against your attested lines after three attempts, the page says so plainly and nothing is produced. Try again asks for another attempt; it will still refuse anything it cannot verify. A refusal is Role Scout keeping its promise, not a fault in your resume.

The cover letter

Written from your attested resume and this posting, then checked claim by claim. Same refusal rule. Generate again writes a fresh letter; Download PDF or Download Word saves it to send with your application.

9. Step 6: Track your application

The Applications page is a board with five columns: Applied, Interview, Offer, Hired, Closed. Drag a card, or use the status dropdown; both do the same thing. A List view shows the same applications as full cards, one under the other.

  • Each card shows the role, employer, the date it entered its column, how many times your shared link was opened, and whether readers said the verified banner made it more credible.
  • A card in Applied for seven days with no opens shows a quiet nudge to follow up.
  • Moving a card into Interview builds an interview pack for that role automatically.
  • Notes are private to you. Add an application records a role you applied for outside Role Scout.

10. Step 7: Prepare for the interview

The interview pack

The pack opens with a readiness panel: questions practised, whether your latest attempt was grounded, whether it met all four criteria, and whether your latest spoken answers stayed within two minutes. It fills as you practise.

SectionWhat it holds
Likely questionsWhat this employer is likely to ask, from the posting. Each has a Practise this pill.
Talking pointsYour strongest attested facts for this role, each with its evidence line.
Honest gapsThe same gaps shown on your tailored resume, one by one. For each: the question they are likely to ask, what you can truthfully say, and, where nothing on your attested resume supports it, the line You cannot claim this yet.
Ask themQuestions worth asking the employer.

Practising an answer

Press Practise this on any likely question, or open a question of your own. You can type your answer or speak it; when you speak, the browser writes a transcript, and you should read and correct the transcript before pressing Check, because speech recognition mishears names. The check reads your answer sentence by sentence against your attested resume: a sentence it can trace shows in teal, and a sentence it cannot trace is marked in amber with the nearest attested fact beside it, so you see exactly which claim went beyond your resume. It then assesses four criteria, each with a plain reason: grounded on your attested resume, answered the question, gave a specific example, stated a result. You get a count of how many were met, never a grade or a percent, and your words are never rewritten; the answer stays yours. A timer records how long the answer took, with your pace and a reminder that one to two minutes is the range interviewers expect. Every attempt is kept in your practice history, and the readiness panel fills as you practise.

Mock interviews

Start a mock interview runs a timed session through the pack's questions: typed or spoken, all questions in order or five at random. A clock counts each answer and turns amber past two minutes. Next submits the answer for checking and moves on, Skip leaves a question, Finish scores what you answered, End stops the session. The summary reports real counts: how many questions you answered, how many answers were fully on your attested resume, how many met all four criteria, and your times. Each row opens the full result for that answer, so you can retake the ones that stayed open. Every session is saved under Mock interviews with its counts and time, sessions ended early say so, and a session still in progress can be ended and its summary viewed.

Build a new pack clears the pack and builds a fresh one from your current attested resume, usually within minutes.

The 30 60 90 day work plan

On the Work plan tab of an Interview application, Build my plan writes a plan for this exact role in three phases: days 1 to 30 to learn, days 31 to 60 to contribute, days 61 to 90 to own. The plan itself is written in the first person, I and my, because it is yours to hand to the hiring manager; the coaching around it speaks to you. Every action is tied to a requirement in the posting and carries a Draws on note naming the attested facts behind it, or is marked New for you when nothing on your resume covers it yet, so the plan commits to actions rather than claiming experience. Nothing is asserted about the employer beyond the posting; unknowns go into a list of assumptions you will confirm with the manager, and the plan ends with questions worth asking and guidance on how to present it. Download it as a full plan or a one page version, each as PDF or Word; the Word copy exists because you will edit the plan after the manager corrects your assumptions. Build a new plan replaces the current one.

Daily allowances. Thirty practice checks, twenty mock interview sessions and three work plans a day, alongside the ten tailorings and cover letters that share one allowance.

11. Versions and the Active version

Every upload is a version. Attestation is per version. One attested version drives your account at a time.

ControlWhat it does
Version rowsTap a parsed version to review it below. The reviewed row shows Reviewing.
ActiveThe version that drives matching, tailoring, cover letters, interview packs and work plans. By default this is your newest attested version.
Use this versionMakes that attested version the active one. New matches are scored against it. Useful when you keep two true resumes, for example a Canadian one and a home country one, or a resume and a LinkedIn export.
Use newest attested insteadReturns to letting the newest attested version drive everything.

12. The browser extension

Save to Role Scout is a one button extension for Chrome and Edge, in final testing and coming to the Chrome Web Store. On any job posting, press it and Role Scout opens with the posting captured for you to check and save. Until it is in the store, use Tailor for a posting you found on the Matches page, which does the same job by paste.

  1. On a posting (Job Bank, LinkedIn, Indeed, Jobillico, an employer site), click the Role Scout icon in the toolbar, then Capture this posting.
  2. Role Scout opens the supply form with the link, title, employer and text filled, and a banner saying where it was captured from. Check the four fields.
  3. Press Save and open. The posting is scored against your attested resume within a minute, then you can tailor and write a letter for it.
What it never does. It does not fill in forms, submit applications, run in the background, or store anything. The captured text travels inside your browser to the Role Scout page and nowhere else.

13. The daily digest email

Every morning at 08:30, if new roles scored 60 or above for you in the last day, you get one email listing up to five of them with the score and the reason line, and a link to Matches. No email on quiet days, never the same email twice. Turn it off in Preferences.

14. Offline, waiting, and what the app tells you

  • Waiting. Every wait (reading a resume, scoring, tailoring, writing a letter, building a pack) shows a card with the usual time. If it runs long, the card says so and tells you it is safe to leave the page.
  • Offline. Installed on your phone, Role Scout stays readable without a connection. Anything that saves shows the message You are offline. This action needs a connection. Nothing is queued; press again when you are back online.
  • New version. After an update, a bar offers Reload. Press it once.
  • Tooltips. Hover or tap and hold any button to read what it does, how long it takes, and what it will not do.

15. When something looks wrong

You seeWhat it means and what to do
Could not readThe file has no text layer or is corrupt. Upload the original document, not a scan or photo.
No matches yetEither you have not attested, or nothing in your country matched your target roles. Check Preferences; widen target roles or leave them empty.
Role Scout declined to produce this tailored resumeThe verifier could not confirm every line as true. Read the reason. Often a target role in Preferences is pulling in roles far from your attested experience.
A pack, plan or letter is taking longer than usualLeave the page; it appears when ready. If it is still missing after an hour, use Send feedback.
A version shows Not attested but you expected it to drive matchesOnly attested versions can be active. Review it, edit anything untrue, then attest.
The extension opens Role Scout but the form is emptyReload the extension from chrome://extensions and try again; some sites block reading, in which case copy the posting text into the form.

Send feedback (footer of every page) reaches a person. We read every message.

17. For recruiters, counsellors and career offices

You can use Role Scout today with no account at all, through the verification links your candidates share.

What a verification link proves

  • Every line on the resume you are reading was attested as true by the candidate, on a specific version, on a specific date. The banner names both.
  • Each changed line is marked. Reworded and merged lines trace to the attested lines behind them; Show all sources reveals them. A title mapped line keeps the candidate's original title in parentheses.
  • Lines a former manager or colleague confirmed carry that confirmation.
  • If the candidate replaces or turns off the link, it stops working. What you see is what they chose to show you now.

One thing you can do on the link

At the bottom of a shared resume, the question Did the verified banner change how you read this application? has one button. Pressing it tells the candidate that a reader found the verification credible. It is anonymous and it is the only thing the page records.

What Role Scout does not do, which matters to you

  • It never applies on a candidate's behalf, never fills employer forms, and never feeds answers during an interview. Every application you receive through it is the candidate's own.
  • It never invents a claim. A candidate cannot use it to inflate a resume; it refuses.
  • It never shows you candidates who did not share with you.

What a recruiter workspace would add

Organization seats are planned for staffing firms, newcomer centres and career offices. The five things on the table, in the order we think you would value them:

  1. Verified shortlist. Candidates who share with you appear as a list: target role, NOC code, verification state, last attested date. Candidates opt in by sharing; nothing is scraped.
  2. Role brief. Paste a client's posting once; every candidate on your shortlist can tailor against it, giving you ten verified resumes for one role in an afternoon.
  3. Request a verified resume. Send a candidate outside Role Scout an invite; they sign up, attest and share back.
  4. Gap view. For a role brief, which coverage gaps recur across your shortlist, so you can tell the client honestly what the market has.
  5. Seat billing per recruiter, with published pricing, no hidden tiers and stated refund terms.
Tell us which one you would pay for first. That answer sets the seat price. Write to the address on postaratrend.ca or use Send feedback inside the app.
